Definition: from G2725; to be a plaintiff, i.e. to charge with some offence:--accuse, object.
BiblicalUsage: To accuse is to bring the charge, and Jesus says Moses is the one who accuses them, and the accuser of the brethren is cast down, and the chief priests accused Him before Pilate and He answered nothing, and Tertullus accused Paul before Felix with flattery. The word runs from the courtroom to the throne of God, and the accuser is always busy, but the Advocate is busier still.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the accuser's voice is loud, but the Advocate's blood speaks better things. I hold that Moses accuses those who trust in Moses and miss Christ, and I will trust in Christ instead.
